title: K001: Add 15 new endpoint handlers to mock API
description:
**Size:** 🏗️ large
**Category:** testing
**Priority:** critical
**Source:** Proposed for 'With the latest commits/features, E2E tests were added'

Add 15 new route handlers to test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go matching all agent-used API endpoints not yet mocked. Each handler validates HTTP method (returns 405 otherwise), increments its dedicated atomic.Int64 counter, stores the last request body in a mutex-protected map, and returns a minimal fixture response (204 or appropriate JSON). New handlers: deregister, keys/rotate, capabilities, endpoint, drift, secrets/{key}, report, executions/{eid}/ack, executions/{eid}/result, metrics, logs, audit, artifacts/{ver}/{os}/{arch}, tunnels/{sid}/ready, tunnels/{sid}/closed, integrity/violations. Add 15 new AssertionCounters fields (DeregisterCount, KeyRotateCount, CapabilitiesCount, EndpointCount, DriftCount, SecretsCount, ReportCount, ExecutionAckCount, ExecutionResultCount, MetricsCount, LogsCount, AuditCount, ArtifactCount, TunnelReadyCount, TunnelClosedCount, IntegrityViolationCount) serialized in /test/assertions JSON. Add request body capture infrastructure: map[string][]byte on Server struct (mutex-protected), plus GET /test/last-request/{endpoint} control endpoint returning raw captured bytes.

**Rationale:** Only 7 of 22 endpoints are mocked. The agent calls 15 additional endpoints that silently fail or get 404 during E2E tests, meaning capabilities reporting, drift detection, observability forwarding, execution lifecycle, and tunnel signaling are completely untested in integration. This is the foundation all other features depend on.

**Affected Areas:**
- test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go

requirements.description: The mock API SHALL provide handlers for all 15 missing agent-used endpoints that increment dedicated atomic counters

tasks.title: Add 15 new atomic.Int64 counters to Server struct and expand AssertionCounters (REQ-001, REQ-007)
tasks.description: Add 15 new atomic.Int64 fields to the Server struct: deregisterCount, keyRotateCount, capabilitiesCount, endpointCount, driftCount, secretsCount, reportCount, executionAckCount, executionResultCount, metricsCount, logsCount, auditCount, artifactCount, tunnelReadyCount, tunnelClosedCount, integrityViolationCount. Expand AssertionCounters with corresponding int64 fields and snake_case JSON tags (deregister_count, key_rotate_count, capabilities_count, endpoint_count, drift_count, secrets_count, report_count, execution_ack_count, execution_result_count, metrics_count, logs_count, audit_count, artifact_count, tunnel_ready_count, tunnel_closed_count, integrity_violation_count). Update Assertions() method to load all 19 counters. Write test: TestAssertions_InitialZero verifies all 19 fields are 0 on fresh server (extend existing test).

tasks.title: Add request body capture infrastructure to Server struct (REQ-004, REQ-006)
tasks.description: Add to Server struct: lastRequests map[string][]byte and lastRequestsMu sync.RWMutex. Initialize map in New(). Add helper method captureBody(endpointName string, r *http.Request) ([]byte, error) that reads the full body via io.ReadAll, stores raw bytes in lastRequests under mutex write lock, and returns the bytes for further processing by the handler (handler will wrap them in bytes.NewReader for json.Decoder). Add helper method LastRequestBody(endpoint string) ([]byte, bool) for programmatic access. Add imports: 'io', 'bytes', 'sync'. Write test: TestLastRequestBody_InitiallyEmpty, TestLastRequestBody_StoredAfterCapture.

tasks.title: Add GET /test/last-request/{endpoint} control endpoint (REQ-004)
tasks.description: Add handleLastRequest handler: reads {endpoint} path value, acquires read lock on lastRequestsMu, looks up lastRequests[endpoint]. If not found, return 404 JSON {"error": "no captured request for endpoint"}. If found, write 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and raw bytes. Register route: 'GET /test/last-request/{endpoint}' in registerRoutes(). Write tests: TestLastRequest_Returns404WhenNoCapturedBody, TestLastRequest_ReturnsCapturedBody (POST to an endpoint, then GET /test/last-request/{endpoint} and verify bytes match).

implementation_notes:
**Architecture:** All changes are confined to test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go and mockapi_test.go. The pattern is established: each handler is a method on *Server, uses atomic counters for thread-safe counting, uses writeJSON/methodNotAllowed helpers, and returns fixture data from internal/api types.

**Body Capture Pattern:** Add captureBody(name string, r *http.Request) ([]byte, error) that does io.ReadAll(r.Body), stores bytes in lastRequests map under sync.RWMutex, and returns bytes. Handlers that need JSON decoding wrap returned bytes in bytes.NewReader for json.NewDecoder. This is a read-then-decode pattern that avoids reading the body twice.

**204 vs 200 Decision:** Endpoints where the client sends nil as the response pointer (doRequest with nil resp) in endpoints.go get 204: deregister, capabilities, drift, report, ack, result, metrics, logs, audit, tunnel_ready, tunnel_closed, integrity_violations. Endpoints where the client expects a response struct get 200 with JSON: keys/rotate (KeyRotateResponse), endpoint (EndpointResponse), secrets (SecretResponse), artifacts (binary stream, 200 with octet-stream).

**Deregister Special Case:** The client passes nil request body (endpoints.go:69), so deregister handler should NOT attempt JSON decoding. Just capture body (which may be empty), increment counter, return 204.

**Artifact Special Case:** Not a JSON endpoint. Returns Content-Type application/octet-stream with a small static byte slice. No JSON encoding.

**Key Files:** test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi.go (main implementation), test/e2e/mockapi/mockapi_test.go (tests), internal/api/types.go (request/response types to use), internal/api/endpoints.go (reference for HTTP methods, paths, and which endpoints expect response bodies).

**Import additions for mockapi.go:** 'bytes', 'io', 'sync' (sync already partially used via sync/atomic).

**Import additions for mockapi_test.go:** none expected (already imports all needed packages).

**Pitfalls:** (1) MetricBatch, LogBatch, AuditBatch are type aliases for slices (e.g., MetricBatch = []MetricPoint), not struct types. JSON decoding into a slice still works with json.Decoder but the variable must be declared as the slice type. (2) Go 1.22 ServeMux method patterns are strict: 'POST /path' only matches POST; the fallback '/path' without method catches everything else. Both must be registered. (3) 204 responses must not call writeJSON — use w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent) directly.
